## Grok Review Comment

🛑 **One must-fix, otherwise a clean, well-split change.**

The `-w`/`-O` feature itself is good work. `secrets.rs` is now split into `target`, `existing`, `sink` and `sops/suffix`, each with one job, so naming lives in one place. Decrypt runs fully in memory before the target is touched, so a failed decrypt can't truncate a file. Backups never overwrite each other. The guard test `every_flattener_declares_the_destination_group` is a nice touch. CI and codecov patch are green.

🛑 **`--non-interactive` now means "yes to everything" for every command.** `lib.rs` feeds `cli.global.non_interactive` into `with_assume_yes`, and `approve` and the break-glass ceremony now ask `ui.assumes_yes()` instead of checking only `SOPSY_ASSUME_YES`. The flag's own help still says *"Disable all interactive prompts; fail instead of asking"*. So `sopsy -y approve alice`, or any CI job with `--non-interactive`, now **auto-vouches a key without the out-of-band check** instead of failing. The "press ENTER to confirm the key is stored safely" step is skipped the same way. That removes a trust gate as a side effect of a file-writing feature. Fix: keep "don't prompt" and "assume yes" as separate inputs. Either add a real `--yes` (and stop aliasing it to `--non-interactive`) or scope the new assume-yes to `encrypt`/`decrypt` only. Leave `approve` and the ceremony on the env-var opt-in, and add a test that `--non-interactive approve` still fails.

🤔 **Answering "No" on decrypt still overwrites** (after a backup). That follows D5, but "Overwrite? No" that then overwrites will surprise people. I'd change the prompt to say what will happen, e.g. *"`.env` exists. Replace it (No keeps a backup first)?"*

🤔 **Plaintext file permissions.** `fs::write` creates a new `.env` with the umask default (usually 0644). Consider creating it 0600 on Unix. Backups made with `fs::copy` keep the old file's mode, which is fine.

🤔 **Backups outside the `.env.*` ignore rule.** `decrypt config.yaml.encrypted -w -O` leaves `config.yaml.2026-…bak`, which `init`'s `.gitignore` doesn't cover. Worth adding `*.bak` to the patterns `init` writes.

🤔 `.plans/…/state.json` adds 644 lines of tool state to the repo. Fine if that's intended, but it's noise in the diff.

— Alan Turing
